content_label.what_it_shows: A beige CRT monitor with a keyboard on a wooden desk in a dim, warm-lit room, with a slow camera drift. The monitor screen is blank and dark for the whole inspected range.
content_label.what_it_does_not_show: It does NOT show a boot, a power-on, POST, a memory count, a BIOS screen or any OS. No PC case or tower is visible anywhere in frame, so no CPU is visible and none can be identified.
content_label.editorial_use: Period-setting cutaway only. Never label this clip a boot. Never caption or imply 'Pentium' over it.
content_label.hardware_markings_legible_at_full_resolu: The monitor bezel reads 'ViewSonic' (lower bezel) with the ViewSonic bird logo and an 'E70' model marking (upper-right bezel). These identify a monitor make and model only, not a CPU, a system or a date. No date, serial, BIOS text or OS marking is legible anywhere in the frame. The 'Pentium-era' framing therefore remains unverified.
content_label.other_props: Two audio cassettes rest on top of the monitor; a rotary telephone, a folding camera, a glass flask and a foil-wrapped object sit on the desk.
